name: Are there size limits for foundation-based tiny homes in Escondido?

mainEntity.name: Are there size limits for foundation-based tiny homes in Escondido?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, in Escondido, foundation-based tiny homes, often built as Accessory Dwelling Units (ADUs), are subject to specific size limits. While regulations can vary, typically a detached ADU has a maximum size of 1,200 square feet, and an attached ADU is limited to 50% of the existing primary dwelling's floor area or 1,200 square feet, whichever is less. There are also minimum size requirements, usually around 150-220 square feet to qualify as an independent living unit. Always confirm current regulations with the City of Escondido's Planning Department before starting design.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Escondido, foundation-based tiny homes (ADUs) typically have a maximum size of 1,200 sq ft and a minimum of 150-220 sq ft.
